https://www.politico.eu/article/ursula-v.text: The Belgrade funeral for war criminal Ratko Mladić contradicts “the values underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union,” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Tuesday. Several Serbian ministers and military leaders attended the ceremony honoring Mladić, who died on Aug. 27 while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. Serbian Orthodox Patriarch Porfirije, a close ally of Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić, led the service and said Mladić’s name “would remain in the memory and prayers of the Serbian people.” Advertisement Advertisement Mladić was the commander of the Bosnian Serb Army during the 1992-95 Bosnian War and was found responsible for the Srebrenica genocide, in which more than 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys were killed in July 1995. The Serbian government said that it had no hand in organizing the funeral, however Mladić’s body was flown to Serbia on a government plane and his coffin was escorted by members of the Serbian Armed Forces. “The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable,” von der Leyen said , adding that “they demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe’s recent history.” “The images from Ratko Mladić’s funeral yesterday in Belgrade were shocking,” wrote European Council President António Costa. “Ratko Mladić was a convicted war criminal. He was responsible for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.” The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas struck an similarly hard line, calling the public glorification of Mladić “an affront to the memory of the victims” and warning that “true reconciliation cannot be built on revisionism, the denial of genocide or the honouring of perpetrators.” Serbia, which is an EU candidate country, has not opened a new negotiating chapter with the bloc since December 2021. The process is blocked by eight member countries over its rule-of-law record and its refusal to sanction Russia for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. This story has been updated with comments from Kaja Kallas. Milena Wälde contributed to this report. Advertisement Advertisement

http://en.people.cn/n3/2026/0905/c312369.text: Home Opinion PD Voice Politics Foreign Affairs Business World We Are China Society Culture Sci-Tech Video Photo Sports Travel Military Life Exclusive Specials Languages Chinese Japanese French Spanish Russian Arabic Korean German Portuguese Swahili Italian Kazakh Thai Malay Greek Vietnamese Urdu Hindi Archive New direct air route links China, Romania and Croatia BUCHAREST, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Air China operated its maiden flight on the new route connecting China's Beijing with Bucharest of Romania, and Zagreb of Croatia, on Friday, restoring direct flights between China and Romania after years of suspension and opening the first direct connection with Croatia. Operating under flight numbers CA913 and CA914, the route departs from Beijing Capital International Airport with a stopover in Bucharest before arriving in Zagreb. Services run three times a week on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, with Airbus A330 aircraft deployed during the initial phase. Bucharest is among the most populous inland city in the Balkans and Romania's political, economic and cultural center. Zagreb, whose history dates back to the 11th century, is a major cultural, tourism and economic hub in Croatia. Calin Mitri, director-general for Global Affairs at the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said in his speech at the launch event held Friday afternoon that in today's world of deeply intertwined economies, direct air connectivity is not merely an improvement in transportation convenience, but also a strong support for international cooperation. He added that the launch of the new route also provides a valuable platform for both sides to exchange experience in airport development, digital transformation, talent cultivation and the application of new technologies. Chen Feng, China's Ambassador to Romania, said that the resumption of regular direct passenger flights between China and Romania is a shared aspiration of the Chinese and Romanian peoples and the result of long-term joint efforts by both sides. "It is expected to help further strengthen bilateral economic and trade cooperation, deepen cultural and people-to-people exchanges, promote mutual understanding, and inject fresh momentum into the sustained and healthy development of China-Romania relations," Chen added. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images US Senate Senate Republicans block Democratic effort to end US war with Iran GOP stymies House-passed war powers resolution as conflict passes 200-day mark with 19 US service members killed Joseph Gedeon and Chris Stein in Washington Thu 24 Sep 2026 15.06 EDT Last modified on Thu 24 Sep 2026 15.08 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Senate Republicans on Thursday blocked a Democratic effort to end the US war with Iran, voting 49-50 against a House-passed war powers resolution as the conflict passed the 200-day mark, with 19 American service members killed. The measure passed the House earlier with bipartisan support. Senate Democrats, led by the minority leader, Chuck Schumer, and the senator Andy Kim of New Jersey, forced the vote under the War Powers Resolution, which allows lawmakers to bring such measures to the floor. In June, the Senate adopted a similar House-passed resolution 50-48, with four Republicans – Bill Cassidy, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul – voting in favor. But a month later, after the ceasefire collapsed, the chamber voted 47-49 against advancing a legally binding joint resolution, with Collins the only Republican in support. After the vote, Ron Wyden, the Democratic senator from Oregon, acknowledged the uphill fight. “We’re going to stay at it until we win,” he said. Wyden said the biggest challenge was senators who were “pretty cautious and looking at the constitutional authority”. Democratic senator Tim Kaine from Virginia echoed that sentiment, saying: “We’re going to keep doing them every week because we see Republican candidates out in the field now starting to change their position.” “We started with one Republican vote, and we have five now,” he said. “So we’ll keep at it.” Still, not all Republicans are convinced on the reasons to end the war. Dan Sullivan, the Republican senator from Alaska, said: “The war powers vote is about removing American forces from the region, and when there are troops in contact, I don’t believe in doing it.” Speaking before the vote, Kim, a former state department official who served in the Middle East, said Americans were “sick and tired of this reckless and expensive war”. “Democrats have taken action. We’ve come to this chamber 11 times in the past 208 days to try to bring this war to an end,” Kim said. He cited a congressional budget office report estimating the war cost nearly $40bn in its first four months, and said at least 19 US service members had been killed and more than 750 injured. Kim also said estimates showed higher petrol prices had cost American households about $900 each since the war began. “Chaos is not a negotiating tactic,” Kim said. “Trump is simply over his head here.” Explore more on these topics US Senate US-Israel war on Iran US foreign policy US Congress US domestic policy Trump administration US military news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text: China has reached an “understanding” with the EU, to avert deterioration in trade tensions after two days of talks in Beijing, according to a Chinese statement. EU trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is due to hold a press conference around 3pm CET, but China says the two sides have agreed a 16 point agreement allowing for a relaxation of restrictions on rare earth exports from China to the EU in return for concessions on electric vehicle exports. China is “willing... to continue facilitating the approval of export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU”, a statement from the Chinese ministry of commerce has said following two days of talks in Beijing. While they acknowledged “differences” between them, the two sides were committed to maintaining trade and to hold a further meeting in March.
